scope: P2 self-disable and explicit restoration; separate from moderation bans, deletion and full account-lifecycle acceptance.
implemented: Additive migration 094 persists self-disable time and a monotonically changing lifecycle version. This state is distinct from platform moderation and is explicitly removed on hard deletion even without foreign-key enforcement.

Account-bound POST /api/users/me/disable requires an active authenticated session, current password, enabled MFA proof, a separate confirmation flag and shared durable security-attempt budget. Bots, stale accounts, oversized/extra JSON and missing confirmation are rejected.

Disable atomically sets offline/last-seen, increments token version, persists disabled state, tombstones every logical sign-in and deletes refresh credentials. Failed database writes roll back every step. Live local-process sockets receive 4001/session_revoked; existing voice-disconnect infrastructure is invoked.

Session creation, refresh and validation reject disabled accounts. A late non-offline presence update cannot revive disabled presence. Normal production login publishes online presence only with successful durable session creation.

A correct-password ordinary login to a disabled account returns ACCOUNT_DISABLED without session rows, presence or cookies. The login form offers an unchecked explicit restore option. Changing identity/password clears that consent; saved desktop credentials do not auto-restore the account.

Explicit restoration still requires the enabled second factor. Restoration, lifecycle/token-version CAS, online state, new logical sign-in and refresh credential commit together. Twelve simultaneous restoration attempts produce one winner. Old credentials remain revoked after restoration.
Password recovery does not clear disabled state. Current password-hash checks inside lifecycle transactions reject stale password proofs, and a platform ban cannot be bypassed by restoration.

TR/EN security form, keyboard-usable confirmation, draft preservation on cancellation/failure, account-generation guards and local-only logout. Disable responses never clear a shared cookie belonging to a later login.

operations.rollout: Preserve a database backup and the existing MFA encryption key. Apply 094 before session/lifecycle-aware binaries. Never run or roll back to a lifecycle-unaware binary against disabled accounts; such an old application would not enforce this state.
operations.meaning: Self-disable blocks login without explicit restore and sets offline; it is not deletion, anonymization, a platform ban, profile hiding or a promise to stop all future email categories. Messages, memberships and server ownership are intentionally retained.
operations.recovery: Password reset is allowed for recovery but does not reactivate. Restore requires a fresh credential login with reactivate=true and enabled MFA. Old tokens are never restoration credentials.
